name: LME49880
tagline: National's late Overture JFET dual (7 nV/√Hz, 0.00003% THD+N): PSOP-only, obsolete, rolled on DIP adapters in Japan.

lineage.note: Launched as the 'Overture E-Series Dual JFET Input' op-amp; siblings LME49720, LME49860, LME49990.
Re-issued as SNAS455C (April 2013); later obsoleted in a process-technology EOL, naming OPA1642 as replacement.

part_numbers.note: Lead-free PSOP-8 with exposed pad. ACTIVE in a 2014 addendum; now OBSOLETE. MRX unconfirmed.
Base National PSOP-8 part/marking; leaded orderable unconfirmed. Shops sell it on DIP-8 adapters.

key_specs.value: JFET (process chosen for low flicker noise)

reputation.summary: A niche part, discussed mainly by Japanese op-amp rollers and in an early diyAudio thread. Japanese users reportedly call it tight, clean and high-resolution, with a 'rich NatSemi tone'. It is PSOP-only, so shops (diyinhk; reportedly Kyoritsu/eleshop, Digit, Bispa) sell it on DIP-8 adapters. No independent measurements found; the datasheet figures support its low-distortion reputation.
typical_uses: DAC I/V and output/LPF stages via DIP-8 adapter
Headphone amps and preamps with DIP-8 sockets
Hi-fi preamp and filter stages (datasheet positioning)
caveats: PSOP-8 with exposed pad only, no DIP; adapters vary in layout, decoupling and pad connection (rail unconfirmed).
Obsolete at TI; supply is old, broker or adapter stock, with rising price and fake risk.
Praise is subjective, from a small mostly Japanese community; no independent measurements.

counterfeit_notes: No LME49880 fake reports found. Since TI obsoleted it (c. 2016–17), 'new' stock is old, broker or adapter-mounted. Genuine parts are PSOP-8 with an exposed underside pad; a padless SOIC-8 is a red flag. Check marking and date-code era.

refuted_claims: Lifecycle 'unknown' or possibly available: refuted; LME49880MR/NOPB is OBSOLETE (TI process EOL), OPA1642 named as replacement.
'SOIC-only': inaccurate; it is an 8-lead PSOP with exposed pad ('SO PowerPAD'). 'SMD only, no DIP' still holds.
